Senses.Note: Dahui's role definition and Fohai's materially different answer are both retained, preventing an exclusively institutional or human-office definition. The former role and vocative targets applied the same label to people in referential and direct-address grammar and are merged. Compare the entries for accomplished person, lineage teacher, visiting a good teacher, general address, and ascending the hall.

Occurrences.Kwic: 善知識！菩提般若之智，世人本自有之。只緣心迷，不能自悟，須假大善知識，示導見性。

Senses.Explanation: A ‘good and knowledgeable person’ is a guide whom practitioners approach, recognize, or are warned to distinguish from a deceptive guide. In Chan records the role is relational: the person directs, tests, or clarifies for someone else. The term occurs 2,832 times in 311 allowlisted texts. Dahui directly says, “those called good teachers guide all beings and cause them to see nature” (夫稱善知識者，引導一切眾生，令見佛性), then describes observing people's capacities and giving teaching as medicine matches illness. He calls such reception and guidance “the proper work a good teacher ought to do” (善知識本分合做底事), and elsewhere mentions “a good teacher's eye for distinguishing people” (善知識辨人眼). The Five Lamps Compendium describes travelling people “visiting good teachers” (參善知識). Another narrative has a student say, “a great good teacher is hard to encounter even across ages; now that I have met one, why begrudge body or life?” (大善知識歷劫難逢，今既得遇，豈惜身命). Asked “what is a good teacher?” (如何是善知識), Fohai replies that lanterns, pillars, cats, and dogs are all called good teachers. The same label supplies the vocative “Good friends!” when speakers address assemblies. Direct address changes who is being hailed, not the lexical kind of label.

Senses.Note: Vocative use: Huineng or Huiyue hails the listening assembly as (善知識). This does not make the listeners their teachers.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source text Platform Sutra of the Sixth Patriarch (六祖大師法寶壇經): Huineng is the exact speaker, hailing the listening assembly as “good friends” before defining the named condition of single conduct.

Occurrences.Kwic: 善知識！一言半句實有起死回生之力、翻窠倒臼之施
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source text Recorded Sayings of Huiyue Xu (晦嶽旭禪師語錄): Huiyue Xu is the exact speaker in a general address, hailing the audience as “good friends” before saying that half a phrase can revive the dead and overturn the old nest.

Senses.Explanation: As a vocative, speakers use this expression to address the listening assembly as “good friends.” The referent is the audience being hailed, not a guide approached for direction. Huineng and Huiyue open direct addresses with the vocative. Huineng’s longer row also separately says that a great good teacher is relied on for guidance; that second use remains evidence for the guide sense.
